findings: Whole test module contains four async unit tests: duplicate with selected provider and matched ID, below-confidence pass-through, missing-ID pass-through, and same-event digest grouping. All LLM responses are deterministic fakes; storage is fake or absent, and AstrBot is stubbed. These tests do not establish semantic accuracy, file-byte equality, image similarity, real provider behavior, timeout/resource bounds, or persistence atomicity. No upstream tests executed.

Parser controls on original module code confirm duplicate="false" becomes True through bool(string), string Infinity confidence is clamped to 1, and fractional/bool group indices are coerced to integers. check validates nonempty match ID but never membership in supplied candidate IDs. Digest application bounds group indices against all original items rather than only the prompt candidate subset. These permissive decisions cannot be used as exact file equality.

LLM await has wait_for but storage lookup/provider resolution precede it without local deadline; synchronous llm_generate invocation also occurs before try. TTL and max candidates have minimum but no upper limit. Failures usually allow content through with a reason; caller policy/persistence still requires review.

AggregateCardImageRenderer is presentation only, with no image duplicate metric. Per-section text lines are bounded but section count and overall image height/allocation have no local ceiling. Output naming uses sanitized digest ID plus whole seconds, allowing same-digest concurrent/same-second overwrite; saves are direct, not atomic. Cache trimming deletes all PNGs beyond newest 20 in supplied output directory, without ownership/name prefix filtering, and suppresses cleanup exceptions. Local-image conversion is eager RGBA without explicit image context lifetime. Do not copy this renderer cleanup policy into a read-only file scanner. No Pillow rendering or cleanup executed.

RSSCommands reset directly awaits storage.clear_seen and reports returned count; it does not itself name a job, coordinate active workers, clear semantic-record state explicitly, or confirm durable commit. Storage/caller registration must be inspected before concluding scope/authorization. rss_probe deliberately shields the task and keeps awaiting it even after repeated cancellation while holding its lock, without a local total deadline. Status recent_error is last dictionary/config iteration entry rather than timestamp maximum; successful time is started_at. Probe formatter strictly allowlists mode/error labels and rejects bool-as-int fields, a useful contrast with permissive semantic result parser. No commands dispatched, resets, network probes or messages sent.

Pinned CI workflow runs only three named test modules (storage, scheduler, aggregate_card_image) under Python 3.12, despite 18 test-named modules in tree. Semantic dedup tests reviewed earlier are not named in this CI invocation; no repository-wide test-discovery gate exists in this workflow. Requirements leave Pillow unpinned and httpx/urllib3 ranged; no locked environment is established by this file. README claims dual KV/JSON restart-safe state and old-item suppression using last_success_time; storage/pipeline evidence is still needed. Roadmap translation planned status lags README implemented translation description, so roadmap is not authoritative implementation proof.

Correction to command-scope uncertainty: clear_seen does explicitly remove semantic_dedup state after version increment. It does not reset feed cursors or dispatch guards, and total reset spans multiple disk/backend awaits rather than one transaction. Legacy v0 content lookup can migrate surviving older records after reset.

Original-class two-instance temporary-state control confirms generic put writes a cached whole-state snapshot without _with_state_lock, overwriting another instance writer_a after writer_b writes. Lock-protected semantic/digest/dispatch operations cannot prevent nonparticipating generic writers. _write_disk_state truncates directly with no atomic rename/fsync, and disk is updated before awaited KV backend, permitting partial failure divergence.

Dispatch claim has expiry but no owner token; late release can remove a newer pending claim after lease expiry. POSIX flock is synchronous inside async methods; on non-POSIX fcntl=None leaves no process lock. TTL index/cache/global records have no independent count budget. These remain scoped observations, not a production crash/concurrency suite.

All 13 original storage tests passed in isolated temporary cwd. They cover restart readback, legacy migration, TTL extension/pruning, link normalization, single-instance claim/release/confirm, digest archive/status and semantic reset. They contain no stale concurrent generic writers, crash during direct JSON truncation, disk/KV split failure or expired-lease owner test; therefore passing results do not contradict the reproduced stale-write loss.

Synthetic original-parser controls confirm fallback GUID hashes only title|published: distinct summaries with same title and missing IDs/dates collide. RSS root namespace is stripped for detection, but unqualified channel/item find misses namespace-qualified RSS children; control returns zero items. RDF is unsupported by this parser branch. max_new_items slices source order after parsing whole XML, not a memory/CPU bound. XML/parse exceptions are logged and skipped; caller must distinguish empty feed from failed parsing. These are event identifiers, not content-byte equality. No external feeds fetched.

Five original parser tests pass; they cover images, media flags, list slicing, Atom and Twitter normalization, not reproduced fallback-ID collision or namespace-qualified RSS. Fetcher serially fetches feeds through to_thread, explicitly passes max_bytes=None and max_redirects=None, decodes all bodies as UTF-8 errors=ignore, and turns exceptions into omitted results. 304 detection uses substring in exception text rather than typed HTTP status. Threaded request cancellation does not itself stop synchronous network work. Need source_http review for underlying timeout/redirect semantics. No live requests executed.

Main plugin registers RSS command router with regex only; neither main router nor reviewed RSSCommands contains an explicit administrator permission guard despite README calling commands administrative. Actual framework/global filtering may supply restrictions, so external authorization behavior remains unverified rather than claiming unrestricted deployment access. initialize starts scheduler; terminate awaits scheduler.stop before probe API cleanup, without try/finally, so stop failure can skip probe cleanup. Single normal plugin instance shares one FeedStorage, narrowing reproduced two-instance overwrite risk to multi-instance/coexisting access rather than proving normal single-instance occurrence. No AstrBot runtime, commands or external messaging executed.

HTTP source whole-read narrows earlier redirect statement: max_redirects=None retains standard urllib/httpx defaults, while SOCKS4 manager explicitly uses 20; do not describe it as unlimited redirects. max_bytes=None does read/materialize entire body in all three branches. Positive byte limits return truncated flag and read at most requested+1 logical bytes, with backend decompression distinctions. Timeout is passed to client/request operations, with no shared monotonic total deadline across redirects/retries/body processing. Cross-origin sensitive headers are stripped in each redirect implementation; this is source evidence, not live transport qualification. Query auth rebuild via dict(parse_qsl) collapses duplicate query keys. No network executed.
original_tests_scope: 13 storage and 5 parser original unit tests passed; not complete suite or live AstrBot
